key_insight: Dagger shows that even under strict hard-label, black-box, and backbone-agnostic constraints, GNN model stealing can be made far more effective by separating structural pretraining from class-balanced classifier tuning.
engineering_relevance: This work highlights a realistic security risk for GNN-as-a-Service systems and suggests concrete defenses must account for limited-query attacks, not just idealized soft-label threat models.
method: Phase 1: pretrain with decoupled information propagation to retain neighborhood context on sparse or isolated nodes.
Use manifold-level node mixup to generate smoother supervision and improve boundary learning from hard labels.
Phase 2: freeze the encoder and fine-tune the classifier with class-balanced sampling plus logit adjustment to handle query imbalance.
evidence_signal: Across four benchmark graphs and four GNN backbones, Dagger achieved up to 18.16% higher fidelity while using 12.23× fewer queries than the strongest baseline.
watch_item: The attack assumes the adversary can still collect enough representative hard-label queries; performance may depend on graph structure and class coverage under very tight budgets.
paper_title: Dagger: Decoupling-based Model Stealing Attack against Graph Neural Networks
